text: [serious] As American forces landed, his commander, Major Yoshimi Taniguchi, made him a promise. [softly] Whatever happens, we'll come back for you. A few months later, World War Two ended. [sadly] But no one came. [curious] Leaflets fell from planes saying the war was over. Onoda decided they were fake. Newspapers were left for him. Letters from his family. He believed none of it.

[somber] So he stayed hidden in the jungle with a few other soldiers, still fighting his war. [serious] And that war was real for the people of Lubang. Over the years, Onoda's group killed local islanders. As many as thirty, by some accounts. [sad] One by one, his companions were gone. By 1972, Onoda was alone.
